title: Deployment risk profile and onboarding runway guide
author: Marisol Vega
content:
Overview:
This guide defines a risk-based onboarding profile and an operational runway for private (VPC and on-prem) deployments of the Redwood runtime. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Field Operators, and the Private Deployments engineering teams who run or validate customer installations. The goal is to align expectations, enumerate acceptance criteria, and provide a prescriptive, time-boxed plan that reduces operational surprises during the first 30 days after handoff.

Why this guide exists:
- Private deployments have heterogeneous environments (network, KMS, on-prem hardware) that significantly influence risk.
- A standardized risk profile lets us: prioritize validation work, set realistic SLAs during onboarding, and create automated evidence bundles for compliance customers.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: VPC-connected private deployments and fully air-gapped on-prem installations that run Redwood Private control plane and runtime artifacts.
- Audience: Field engineers, operator teams, customer SREs, sales engineers, and security reviewers.

High-level approach:
1) Classify customer risk across five domains: Network, Cryptography & Keys, Telemetry & Evidence, Capacity & Performance, and Change/Upgrade Surface.
2) Map a recommended onboarding runway (preflight -> install -> stabilization -> evidence delivery -> handoff) with concrete checkpoints and acceptance gates.
3) Provide templates and operator commands for evidence collection and rollback safety gates.

1) Risk profile matrix (summary):
Table: risk_domain | low | medium | high
- Network | Direct VPC peering with private subnets and predictable RTT (<10ms) | Transit via partner interconnects, occasional MTU or NAT translation | Customer-managed egress proxies, NAT with unknown middleboxes, variable WAN link >100ms
- Cryptography & Keys | KMS available with customer-managed CMKs and recorded rotation policy | KMS present but with limited audit integrations | No central KMS; hardware HSM unavailable or attestation required
- Telemetry & Evidence | Full telemetry (metrics, traces, structured logs), sample retention 90 days | Metrics only; traces sampled at 1% | Minimal telemetry; strict data-minimization or regulatory redaction constraints
- Capacity & Performance | Homogeneous GPU fleet with 10–20% spare capacity and node-level telemetry | Heterogeneous accelerators, 0–10% spare, preemptible instances | Highly constrained GPU budget, mixed architectures with warm/cold pools
- Change & Upgrade Surface | Customer agrees to scheduled maintenance windows and operator access | Limited windows and restricted operator privileges | Dynamic environment where OS/firmware changes without operator notice

Each domain above maps to mitigations and recommended operator actions later in this doc.

2) Onboarding runway (timeline & checkpoints):
- Preflight (T-minus 14 days) 
  - Deliverables: Preflight questionnaire; operator contact roster; temporary SSH bastion and agent certs.
  - Checks: Network diagram received; CIDR ranges, egress routes, and KMS endpoint listed; rack-level power/thermal info for on-prem.
  - Acceptance gate: Network trace test and remote attestation artifact received.

- Install (Day 0 to Day 2)
  - Deliverables: Signed image bundle, operator playbook, and initial model artifact SHA list.
  - Steps (numbered):
    1) Validate images and signatures on-airgap transfer checklist.
    2) Run bootstrap with operator in assisted mode: operator runbook output captured to artifact store.
    3) Smoke test: API responds to /health and sample generate request under 1s for control plane calls.
  - Acceptance gate: All smoke tests pass and a telemetry heartbeat is observed for 1 hour.

- Stabilization (Day 3 to Day 14)
  - Focus: Load profiling, KV-cache warmup, prefix caching validation, and realistic traffic replay.
  - Steps:
    1) Execute synthetic traffic at 30%, 60%, 90% of expected sustained QPS for 6h windows.
    2) Capture latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99) and GPU utilization.
    3) Validate autoscaler behavior and preemption handling for preemptible nodes.
  - Acceptance gate: No more than 5% error amplification (errors per minute increase) under 90% load; p99 under customer SLO threshold.

- Evidence delivery & compliance (Day 7 to Day 21)
  - Deliverables: Evidence bundle containing logs, telemetry config, KMS attestation, and test reports.
  - Items required for regulatory customers: egress proofing, redaction templates, signed operator runbooks.
  - Acceptance gate: Customer and security reviewer sign-off on evidence bundle.

- Handoff & burn-in (Day 14 to Day 30)
  - Final tasks: Finalize runbook for daily operator checks, schedule first QBR, and place SLO error budget in monitoring.
  - Acceptance gate: Operational readiness review completed; handover meeting recorded and owner assigned.

3) Concrete acceptance criteria and checklists (operator checklist):
- Network checklist (each item must be yes/no):
  - BGP/peer config validated (if used).
  - MTU and path MTU discovery verified for model artifact transfer.
  - TCP keepalives and idle timeouts configured per guide: idle_timeout <= 15m for long-lived KV streams.
  - Cross-AZ path measurements recorded and baseline p50/p99 RTT.

- KMS & keys checklist:
  - CMK created for tenant and key policy contains operator principal.
  - Key rotation schedule documented and a test rotation executed in staging.
  - HSM attestation (if present) exported and stored in evidence bundle.

- Telemetry & evidence checklist:
  - Metrics: Rediscovery probes, token-level counters, per-model p99 latencies.
  - Traces: Sample rate configured, at least one end-to-end trace captured.
  - Logs: Structured logs (JSON) enabled and ingestion verified to evidence bucket with retention policy.
  - Evidence: Bundle includes timestamps, SHA256 for artifacts, and operator script logs.

- Capacity & performance checklist:
  - Model artifact locality verified (weights cached locally vs. remote).
  - KV cache hit-rate measured and documented.
  - GPU telemetry available at node level and exported to metrics backend for 90 days.

4) SLOs, thresholds, and safety gates (recommended defaults):
- SLOs (can be tightened during contract negotiation):
  - Control plane API availability: 99.95% monthly
  - Serving p99 latency (short sequences): <= 350ms for small models; <= 1.2s for large models (customer defined)
  - Ingest and telemetry: metrics latency < 30s for critical counters
- Safety gates for upgrades and rollback:
  - Canary window: 1 hour at 5% traffic with synthetic checks.
  - Automatic rollback condition: error rate increases by >150% over baseline for two consecutive 5-minute windows, or p99 latency degrades by >2x.
  - Manual rollback gate: any security-critical certificate or KMS failure.

5) Upgrade and rollback playbook (short):
- Pre-upgrade: Confirm preflight snapshot is present; record KV-cache size and in-flight sessions snapshot.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 60 minutes, run automated acceptance prompts and evals against canned prompt set.
- Monitoring hooks: add smoke queries for small, medium, long contexts and embed them into canary checks.
- Rollback steps (if gate violated):
  1) Disable new model/variant routing at the load balancer.
  2) Revert runtime artifact to previous SHA from artifact store.
  3) Restart minimal set of nodes (preserve KV state if possible).
  4) Run smoke tests and share evidence bundle with customer contact.

6) Telemetry evidence bundle (template of contents):
- file: evidence/metadata.txt -> short key-value manifest (install id, operator, timestamps).
- file: evidence/metrics.csv -> downsampled metrics at 1s granularity for critical counters.
- file: evidence/traces.jsonl -> representative traces for successful and failed requests.
- file: evidence/image-shas.txt -> signed SHAs for runtime and model artifacts.
- file: evidence/attestation.txt -> KMS/HSM attestation and operator signature.

7) Operator commands & snippets (examples):
- Capture a KV cache snapshot (example CLI):
  redwood-ops kv snapshot --tenant tenant-a --out /tmp/tenant-a-kv.snapshot

- Collect metrics window (one-line):
  redwood-ops metrics export --from now-2h --to now --output evidence/metrics.csv

- Basic smoke test (curl):
  curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://private-api.example.local/v1/generate -d '{
    "input": "short hello",
    "max_tokens": 16
  }' | jq '.'

8) Ownership and escalation model:
- Primary owner: Private Deployments Field Team (oncall: pd-field@redwood.ai).
- Escalation path: Field Engineer -> Private Deployments Eng -> Eng SRE -> CTO on-call (security or data-loss incidents).
- Contact template to include when escalating: install id, artifact SHAs, relevant telemetry windows (ISO8601 timestamps).

9) Examples of mitigations per risk domain:
- Network high-risk: deploy an operator-side forwarder in customer network and enable packet capture during preflight for diagnostic replay.
- KMS high-risk: require attested HSM and use short-lived session keys for operator tasks; deny operator console access to keys.
- Low telemetry: increase synthetic probes and sample a larger fraction of requests for first 72 hours to accelerate signal collection.

10) Appendix: smoke test prompt set (short):
- Task 1: "Summarize the following sentence: Redwood inference makes serving predictable."
- Task 2: "Convert to JSON: {name: 'Alice', action: 'login'}"
- Task 3: "Long-context stability: repeat the word 'token' 512 times and ensure system responds without OOM."

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Marisol Vega (Private Deployments documentation).
- Reviews scheduled: quarterly or after any major change to the install flow.
- Change log: record high level changes in the top of this document and push updated evidence templates to the artifact store.

Related resources:
- See related preflight questionnaire and evidence templates in the customer requirements library.
- Use the day-2 operator runbooks for ongoing operational tasks after handoff.

If you are implementing this guide for a specific customer, use the Risk Profile matrix to generate a two-page summary for the contract and ensure Security signs the evidence bundle before production traffic is allowed.
